title: Music Player
mainDescription:
A web-based music player application that allows users to listen to their favorite songs, create playlists, and customize their listening experience.

The app has:
secondaryDescription:
• its backend built with .NET Core to get the songs locally and serve an API with features like streaming songs, getting albums / artists, etc.
  • its frontend powered by Angular, which features an intuitive, user-friendly interface.

title: code-cluster
mainDescription:
An archive of problems which tackle subjects such as: dynamic programming, data structures or programming done in languages like: c++, python, java, typescript, etc.

From getting error values of a dataset by training a linear regression model, to training a logistic regression model for predicting digits from images, the repository covers a wide range of topics. Other examples would be a simulation for a movie recommendation platform in java and an implementation of pushdown automata algorithm in c++.

title: iungOreal
mainDescription:
A microservice-based social platform designed to connect users with local outdoor events via interactive mapping (its name is a wordplay for 'going outside', where “iungo” means “to connect” in Latin).

Users can: post and comment on made posts, discuss in private / group / regional chats, update their profile to their liking and many other useful interactions.
secondaryDescription:
• Core Architecture: Built using a Spring Boot server-side and Angular client-side architecture. Integrated Leaflet for dynamic spatial data and AWS SDK for cloud connection.
  • Real-Time Interaction: Created real-time communication protocols using StompJS WebSockets to support private, group, and regional chatting.
  • Quality & Security: Leveraged the spring-boot-starter ecosystem for robust security and database management, ensuring high reliability through comprehensive unit and integration testing with JUnit, Mockito, and an H2 in-memory database.

title: InfOpescuit V2
mainDescription: This was the foundational desktop gateway built to solve the mundane, error-prone manual data entry for customer check-ins and end-of-day accounting at fishing lakes. It served as the initial, highly optimized payment and barcode-scanning engine distributed to lake managers.
secondaryDescription:
• Core Engine & UI: Developed a robust desktop application in Python (compiled in C++ to strictly optimize runtime execution speeds), featuring a Tkinter interface designed to restrict unnecessary data exposure.
  • Automation & Security: Engineered an automated OpenPyxl reporting pipeline for custom .xlsx/XML generation. Secured operations using HMAC, asymmetric encryption keys, and JWTs.
thirdDescription: This foundational system replaced manual spreadsheet manipulation by the lake managers, accelerating data entry speeds by at least 12 times and reducing human error rates by a factor of 20. This massive operational upgrade proved the product's market value and justified the client's investment in the V3 cross-platform expansion.

title: StreetArt Platform
mainDescription: Event organizers needed to digitize a slow, heavily paper-based venue booking process. The goal was to build a centralized platform that allowed committees to efficiently approve street artists, while enabling citizens to easily discover live local events via interactive maps.
secondaryDescription:
• Backend & Database: Developed a secure booking API using Spring Boot and a MySQL database via JPA (hosted on AWS RDS), translating stakeholder requirements into a strict, role-based authorization system through Spring Security.
  • Frontend & Storage: Built an interactive Angular client featuring a Leaflet map integration and AWS S3 as object storage to drive user discovery of local artists and venues.
  • Infrastructure: Designed a cost-effective, containerized infrastructure using Docker and deployed it on a DigitalOcean Ubuntu VM. Configured an nginx reverse-proxy to handle request redirection, HTTPS enforcement, and rate-limiting, balancing application performance needs with deployment budgets.
  • Quality Assurance: Guaranteed system stability by achieving high code coverage using JUnit 5 / Mockito and Jasmine / Karma.
thirdDescription: This architecture successfully replaced a fragmented, manual pipeline with a highly available digital platform, accelerating the committee approval process and bridging the gap between local artists and their communities.

title: InfOpescuit V3
mainDescription: As the product outgrew the initial desktop application, the client required a highly maintainable, modern, and cross-platform ecosystem. The challenge was to deliver a significantly improved, intuitive user experience across both Windows and Android tablets, while expanding on the complex hardware and spreadsheet integrations established in the legacy system to support the diverse operational demands of various fishing lakes.
secondaryDescription:
• Cross-Platform Architecture: Engineered a scalable, next-generation application in Flutter, successfully modernizing the legacy UI and drastically reducing the client's future update and maintenance overhead across different operating systems.
  • Complex Data & Hardware Integration: Built sophisticated native spreadsheet manipulation (flutter_excel) and dynamic table rendering (trina_grid). Integrated barcode generation, allowing lake managers to instantly view, modify, and sync Excel sheets directly within the app's localized environment.
  • Dynamic Business Logic: Engineered modular POS flows, integrating real-time cash register synchronization during check-ins/outs. Developed highly configurable modules for membership fees, promotions and reservations to accommodate the lake managers' specific daily workflows.
  • Security Architecture: Migrated and maintained a strict, unified security posture, protecting application data and authentication flows using HMAC, asymmetric encryption keys, and JWTs.
thirdDescription: By successfully transitioning the product to this modern framework, the platform provides the client with a highly flexible, future-proof software product, while empowering the lake managers with a system that looks better, scales faster, and runs natively on any device they require.

title: AsigurAZ
mainDescription: Stakeholders needed a unified system to simplify the car insurance purchasing pipeline, requiring secure cross-platform access and fail-proof payment synchronization.
secondaryDescription:
• Frontend: Engineered a responsive, cross-platform user interface in Flutter, translating client usability requirements into a seamless multi-device experience.
  • Backend & Architecture: Orchestrated complex API synchronizations between a serverless Node.js / GCP backend, 24Broker's external server, Netopia payment webhooks, and Mailtrap for transactional emails, ensuring transactional reliability for external insurance policy generation.
  • AI & Data Extraction: Proposed and implemented a Gemini API OCR pipeline, resolving a major business bottleneck by automating data extraction and parsing of Romanian car registration certificates.
  • Security & Infrastructure: Aligned architecture with strict data privacy requirements by hardening endpoints via JWTs, App Check, and GCP Secrets Manager, mitigating abuse with Upstash Redis through rate limiting.
thirdDescription: The final application drastically reduced operational overhead for the insurance agent, while giving end-users a seamless, zero-friction way to buy and track policies directly from their devices.
